result.reason: H1 (generic-host-checkpoint) persists a compact semantic checkpoint so future Agents can resume without rereading full history, with many fields reconstructable from current owner truth and a smaller subset holding participant-selected commitments or unresolved identities unavailable elsewhere. The reconstructable majority connects to T4/T6: a read-only projection over owner-native truth avoids duplicating authority and is reusable only while owners remain independent. The smaller subset of non-reconstructable private commitments maps to T2, which became TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL specifically because durable owner state with a clear lifecycle and owner was needed to recover private commitments and unresolved external identities after replacement. H1 bundles both a reconstructable projection (bounded value, not itself authoritative) and a genuine durable-state subset for commitments/identities. The evidence does not show independent consumers repeatedly consuming H1 as a stable shared boundary, nor a mature mechanism already owning the full subset; the uniqueness of the commitment/identity subset is real but not yet demonstrated as broadly transferred across heterogeneous owners. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern of T5: it preserves an opaque immutable binding with option-value at a bounded/organizational scope, useful locally but not yet proven as broad transferable capital. It is not NO_CAPITAL because unlike T3/T6 there is a demonstrated non-reconstructable subset (private commitments) that plain retrieval or owner-native projection cannot already serve, so the change has real option value at a bounded scope.

H1 persists a semantic checkpoint so future Agents can resume without rereading history. The evidence pattern distinguishes broad durable-owner state (T2 TRANSFERRED: private commitments/unresolved external identities that survive replacement and have no other authoritative source) from broad shared semantics or writable global authority that duplicates existing truth (T3/T6 NO_CAPITAL), and from bounded/composition-specific reuse that has not yet demonstrated a broad independent consumer schema (T5 SCOPED). H1 is a hybrid: most checkpoint fields are reconstructable from current owner truth (like T6's owner-native projection, which was NO_CAPITAL because a global writable database would duplicate truth), but a smaller subset may contain participant-selected commitments or unresolved identities unavailable anywhere else (like T2's durable owner state). The reconstructable majority does not justify a broad shared checkpoint authority and would duplicate owner truth; the unique minority is the part with real continuity value, but its scope is bounded to participant-selected commitments/unresolved identity recovery rather than the repeatedly-consumed, stable, owner-independent responsibility seen in T2, T4, T7, T8 TRANSFERRED cases. No evidence shows later independent consumption by multiple owners or a stable unowned responsibility for generic checkpoint authority, so it is useful at a bounded option-value/partial scope, matching SCOPED_CAPITAL. It is read-only (persisting and reading back state) and confined to Computing research.

H2 keeps two digest-bound scoped CONNECT paths only as an option alongside ambient networking, which still completes all currently tested useful work. The scoped paths offer a bounded/local advantage (potentially faster on some services, option value under future ambient failure) but impose dedicated services and qualification, and no independent owner or repeated responsibility consumes them as the default. This mirrors T5 (SCOPED_CAPITAL): a real option/preserved-binding advantage at a partial scope, without a second materially independent consumer demonstrating a shared stable boundary, and without the repeated unowned responsibility that T2/T4/T7/T8 showed for TRANSFERRED. It also avoids T6's failure mode (ambient already works, so a new authoritative writable path would duplicate truth) and T3's failure mode (no demonstrated gap in the current baseline). The benefit is conditional on future ambient failure, so it is option-value capital at a bounded scope rather than demonstrated transferred capital.

The holdout change is an option-value mechanism parallel to T5 (configuration-identity). Two scoped digest-bound HTTPS CONNECT paths exist beside ambient networking; ambient already completes all currently tested useful work, and the scoped paths are materially faster only on some services while adding dedicated services and qualification cost. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern where a bounded/partial/option-value mechanism is retained but has not demonstrated broad transferable capital: no independent consumer or repeated responsibility requires scoped egress, and ambient networking remains the working default. It is not NO_CAPITAL because it is explicitly retained for real (though bounded/local) speed advantage and future option value under ambient failure, contrasting with T3/T6 where the mechanism merely duplicated truth or had no demonstrated consumer. It is not TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because no later independent consumption or repeated responsibility evidences a stable reusable scope beyond the bounded optional egress use.

H3 is a model-visible prior about responsibility ownership/feedback, not an externalized shared mechanism. The evidence pattern shows TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL only when later independent consumers reuse a stable, evidenced responsibility (T2 durable owner state, T4 relation semantics, T7 agent-first method, T8 promotion rule). NO_CAPITAL occurs when no independent consumer exists (T3, T6). H3's effect on a later multi-turn objective is described as indirect and dependent on many subsequent policy choices, meaning it is a helpful bounded/option-value adjustment rather than a demonstrably reused stable capability or a demanded shared surface. It most closely matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL case of being useful but only at a local/partial/option-value scope (cf. T1 and T5), since its value is real but not shown to transfer broadly as an independent reusable boundary.

H3 is a model-visible prior (a way of reasoning about responsibility ownership/feedback) carried from earlier Game work into later rescue behavior. Unlike T2 (durable owner state) or T4 (repeated manual joining cost), H3 does not establish a concrete mechanism that survives replacement or a shared consumable relation semantics; it is a heuristic bias whose effect on later objectives is explicitly indirect and depends on subsequent policy choices. Unlike T7/T8, there is no evidence of a second independent consumer or repeated demonstrated responsibility beyond the Game domain itself. The evidence supports value localized to a Game-derived reasoning context, not broad transferable capital — matching SCOPED_CAPITAL rather than TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, while the retained-and-applied nature rules out NO_CAPITAL.

The change is an owner-local, read-only deterministic reducer targeting a single bounded burden (repeated source-history aggregation) with a clear owner (Security) and an exact escape hatch. This matches the pattern of T4 and T5: owner-native read-only projections that reconstruct or compare without claiming authority over shared truth, while owner recovery remains independent of the projection. T4 achieved TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because multiple independent owners and formal evaluation repeatedly consumed the same relation semantics; T5 stayed SCOPED_CAPITAL because only one real non-Evaluation owner composition existed. Here the mechanism is explicitly Security-local, the model still must interpret the projection correctly (no demonstrated independent consumption yet), and there is no evidence of repeated unowned stable responsibility or a second independent consumer. Under T8's promotion rule, a shared semantic boundary requires repeated unowned stable responsibility before promotion, which is not evidenced. Therefore the reducer is useful at a bounded/local projection scope but not yet demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

The change moves an exact, precision-sensitive repeated aggregation out of model reasoning into a deterministic owner-local reducer/projection that the model then consumes. This matches the strongest positive patterns only partially: T4 and T7 succeeded because (1) the mechanism is read-only, rebuildable/owner-native, and avoids duplicating authority, and (2) multiple independent consumers reuse the same relation semantics. Here the mechanism has a clear owner (Security) and an exact, deterministic escape, which fits the 'owner-native projection rather than a new global authority surface' pattern that succeeded in T4 and was prescribed by T8. However, crucially, the change still leaves the model to interpret the projection correctly, so the reduction has not fully replaced reasoning and its transferable value for a second independent consumer is not evidenced. T5 shows that a Computing-composition mechanism with a bounded owner and opaque/deterministic binding is SCOPED until a second real non-Evaluation owner demonstrates a shared schema; likewise T1/T3 show projection-style or graph-style mechanisms stay scoped/failed absent demonstrated independent consumption. Because only Security-local scope is evidenced here and the model-interpretation dependency remains, the change is useful at a bounded local/partial scope but not demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H5 (render-review-prior) closely matches the signature of the TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL examples. Like T4 (observation-minimum) and T7 (agent-first-research-method), it is a bounded, read-only procedure with a direct observable artifact (exact rendered pixels), an unchanged control baseline, and a defined correction path rather than a new authority surface or duplicated truth store. Its intended scope is explicitly later ordinary repeated production work (Web/Studio across pages), i.e., independent later consumption, not a one-off. This contrasts with the NO_CAPITAL cases (T3, T6) which proposed new global/authoritative stores not required by independent consumers, and with the SCOPED_CAPITAL cases (T1, T5) whose shared schema/authority failed to demonstrate a second independent owner. The rule has no new writable authority and no schema to standardize; it is a reusable constraint consumed across heterogeneous later tasks, analogous to T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule), which transferred.

H5 captures a domain-native proof rule (inspect rendered pixels for expression/layout) rather than a new shared mechanism or authority surface. The evidence pattern is: rules that express a stable, repeatedly-consumable judgment boundary transfer when they are consumed by multiple later owners/tasks (T2 durable owner state, T7 agent-first method rule, T8 infrastructure-promotion rule), whereas proposed machinery that duplicates mature authority or lacks an independent consumer does not (T1, T3, T6). H5 has the key transfer markers: a direct observable artifact, a bounded correction path, exact unchanged controls, and an explicitly stated intent for later ordinary Web/Studio production beyond one original page. Unlike T5 (still only one second owner composition), it is a reusable procedure rule analogous to T7/T8, not a schema needing a second owner demo. It does not create a new writable authority or shared kernel, so it avoids the NO_CAPITAL failure mode. Therefore TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is supported.

H6 closely parallels T1, T5, and a key discipline from T8. Like T1 and T5, it externalizes a shared projection over a boundary where mature mechanisms already own the mechanics (native configuration/route affordances), keeps native evidence reachable, is read-only, and deliberately avoids creating a central authority or registry. The repeated reconstruction of route affordances (fresh Agents repeatedly re-deriving them) is the demonstrated consumer, and the proposed surface pays that stated recurring cost with a narrow read-only projection. However, the evidence shows consumption only by Agents within the same Computing/Workstation context, not yet by an independent second owner or by unowned stable responsibility. This matches T5 (a projection consumed by one real owner plus an experiment, not yet a broad shared schema) and the T4 contrast, where multiple independent owners and formal evaluation had to consume the relation to reach TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. Because the surface has a clear bounded read-only option value and paid recurring cost but no demonstrated independent owner or repeated unowned responsibility, it is useful at a local/partial scope, so SCOPED_CAPITAL is the best-evidenced prediction rather than TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL or NO_CAPITAL.

H6 closely matches the pattern that promoted changes to TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL: a recurring heterogeneous pain (fresh Agents repeatedly reconstructing route affordances from raw configuration) is addressed by a run-once, read-only, owner-local projection that leaves all effects/selection to the Agent and keeps native evidence reachable. This mirrors T4 (multiple owners repeatedly pay manual joining cost -> read-only owner exporters plus a rebuildable projection, consumed across owners) and T8 (inherit mature mechanisms, add smallest owner-local read-only projection rather than a shared writable authority). The surface explicitly avoids the failure modes of the NO_CAPITAL cases: it does not create a central capability registry (contrast T6's rejected global writable usage database) and does not impose a new graph authority (contrast T3). The repeated reconstruction burden across fresh Agents is a demonstrated independent consumption signal, not a hypothetical single-owner abstraction. The read-only, no-effect, non-authoritative design means it does not duplicate truth or create a new compatibility surface, which is exactly the bounded projection style repeatedly rewarded in the evidence.

The holdout change (H7) carries the compact Infrastructure Promotion Rule itself as a fixed prompt prior into a later heterogeneous set of decisions, adding no new owner facts. The training evidence shows a strong regularity: a reusable RULE that guides later heterogeneous decisions, with no new authoritative surface and no duplication of truth, transfers as capital. T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule) is the direct precedent — a rule 'intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions' transferred. T7 (agent-first-research-method) is a similar rule/method consumed by the experiment loop and later by Computer self-audit, also transferred. H7 is essentially the same class: a compact, fact-free, read-only prior that is consumed across later decisions, and unlike T3/T6 (which proposed new storage/authority and were NO_CAPITAL), it introduces no new owner facts, no writable database, no shared kernel/authority surface. The only stated risk is 'may bias different model families differently' and that the historical rule may not generalize — but the identical rule already demonstrated stable transferred scope (T8), and the compact/frozen prior is directly consumable by the experiment loop as a decision input, matching the T7/T8 transfer signature of a stable evidenced scope consumed by multiple later independent decisions.

H7 carries the already-promoted Infrastructure Promotion Rule (T8) forward as a fixed prompt prior for later architecture/owner decisions. T8 itself reached TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL as a reusable rule that guides heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions, and H7 is a mechanism that makes that rule persist across a later heterogeneous decision set. However, the key evidence in H7 is explicitly conditional: the held-out change 'adds no new owner facts' and 'may bias different model families differently,' with value only 'expected' if the historical rule genuinely generalizes. This mirrors the SCOPED_CAPITAL patterns in T1 (prototype expresses many semantics but broad authority surface unproven) and T5 (one owner composition works, second owner schema unproven): the change demonstrably reuses an existing capital asset but has not yet shown independent, repeated consumption across different model families or owner contexts. The value is bounded to the case where T8 generalizes to a new heterogeneous set and where bias does not undercut the benefit; no independent consumer or repeated responsibility beyond the single forward-carry has been evidenced. Therefore the later value is useful at a bounded/local/option-value scope rather than demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

The holdout change H8 is a generic calibration procedure that asks, before choosing any disposition, about current consumer, incremental outcome, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, and reopen/deletion, then applies the same checklist to a materially different professional-equipment decision family. This mirrors exactly the pattern that distinguishes TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL in the training evidence: T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule) is a 'reusable rule' guiding 'heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions' and is labeled TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL; T7 (agent-first-research-method) is a bounded method consumed by the experiment loop AND later by Computer self-audit and is TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. In contrast, SCOPED_CAPITAL results (T1, T5) are structures whose later consumer is only a single owner or an unproven second-owner composition, and NO_CAPITAL results (T3, T6) are mechanisms that duplicate or add authority where no independent consumer requires them. H8 is a decision procedure, not a shared mechanism: it produces no new authoritative surface, does not duplicate existing truth, and its value comes from repeated independent consumption across domains. Two independent consumers are evidenced: the original experiment loop (choosing dispositions) and a materially different professional-equipment decision family, plus the rule's intent to generalize to heterogeneous decisions. This repeated independent consumption of the same relation/decision semantics across owners is the defining evidence for TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL.

The holdout change (generic-calibration-checklist) is a reusable procedure/rule that replaces a static prior with a context-driven evidence checklist, explicitly designed to be applied across a materially different professional-equipment decision family. This closely matches two transferred-capital exemplars in the training evidence: T7 (agent-first-research-method), where a bounded method with authority boundary and deletion is consumed by the loop and later by self-audit with owner-controlled promotion, and especially T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule), where a reusable rule intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions earned TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. The key evidence for transfer is repeated independent consumption at a stable evidenced scope: the checklist asks the same current-consumer/incremental-outcome/simpler-baseline/recurring-cost/authority-fit/reopen-deletion questions when choosing a disposition, and is applied to a different decision family, demonstrating later independent consumption beyond the original scope. This distinguishes it from NO_CAPITAL (which describes changes that duplicate existing truth or have no independent consumer, T3/T6) and SCOPED_CAPITAL (which describes changes still tied to one bounded owner record with no second real non-owner composition, T1/T5). The checklist is a read-only procedure with no effect outside Computing research promoted by declaratively defined boundary, and the training evidence shows the generic rule pattern is what transfers.
